items.title: The Eight Bases of Mastery, and What "Mastery" Actually Means — the "Eight Things" Category Closes

items.zh: 又若觀諸色，若如所觀，於初三解脫中而修習者，謂三解脫方便道所攝三勝處也。此中觀外諸色，若小若大、若好若惡、若劣若勝者。謂觀非三摩地所行現所得色。由緣三摩地所行作意不種種現前，故名為勝。於三摩地所行中，奢摩他行名知，毘鉢舍那行名見。如於三摩地所行若知若見，如於彼色已尋思、已了別，如是於外所想非三摩地所行中觀諸色亦爾。
items.en: Further, whether observing forms [in limited or extensive number], or observing them [as bright colours], cultivated within the first three liberations — these are the three bases of mastery comprised within the three liberations as their preparatory path. Herein, observing outer forms — whether small or great, whether pleasant or repulsive, whether inferior or superior — refers to observing form actually obtained [in ordinary experience], not that which operates within meditative absorption. By taking as object what operates within meditative absorption, attention no longer manifests in manifold, uncontrolled ways — hence it is called mastery. Within what operates in meditative absorption, the activity of calm is called knowing, and the activity of insight is called seeing. Just as, with respect to what operates within meditative absorption, there is such knowing and seeing, such investigation and discernment of that form, so too is it likewise with observing forms in what is perceived outside, not operating within meditative absorption.

items.title: The Ninth Numeric Category — Nine Fetters, and the Nine Abodes Encompassing Every Place Any Being Actually Lives

items.zh: 已說八種佛教所應知處。次說九種。謂有九結。如攝事分當廣建立。又有九種生處受生有情，於彼彼處同所居止。謂三界中，除諸惡趣，可厭處故。如前已說。
items.en: The eight-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the nine-thing category. There are nine fetters, to be broadly established in the Compendium of Topics. There are also nine kinds of birthplace in which sentient beings dwell together, each in their own place: within the three realms, excluding only the evil destinies, since these are utterly repugnant places — as already explained.

items.title: A Major Section: The Ten Totalities and the Ten Factors of an Arhat Close "Ten Things" — and With It, the Entire Science of Inner Wisdom

items.zh: 已說九種佛教所應知處。次說十種。謂十遍處。當知即諸解脫所作成就。餘解脫、勝處、遍處，如攝事分當廣分別。又有十無學支，當知無學五蘊所攝。謂戒蘊、定蘊、慧蘊、解脫蘊、解脫知見蘊。如是已說十種佛教所應知處，及前所說佛教所應知處等，當知皆是內明處攝。
items.en: The nine-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the ten-thing category. There are the ten totalities: know that these are precisely what the liberations accomplish. The remaining details of the liberations, bases of mastery, and totalities will be broadly differentiated in the Compendium of Topics. There are also ten factors of one beyond training, comprised, know, within the five aggregates of one beyond training: the aggregate of precepts, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation. Thus the ten-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained, and, together with everything said before it, know that all of it is comprehended within inner wisdom.

items.title: The Second Science Opens: Medicine, Mapped Directly Onto the Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 云何醫方明處？當知此明略有四種。謂於病相善巧，於病因善巧，於已生病斷滅善巧，於已斷病後更不生方便善巧。如是善巧廣分別義，如經應知。
items.en: What is the science of medicine? Know that, briefly, this science has four aspects: skill regarding the marks of illness, skill regarding the cause of illness, skill in eliminating an illness that has already arisen, and skill in the means preventing an eliminated illness from arising again. The broad differentiation of this skill's meaning should be known as found in scripture.

items.title: The Third Science Opens: Logic, and Its Sevenfold Framework

items.zh: 已說醫方明處。云何因明處？謂於觀察義中諸所有事。此復云何？嗢拕南曰：論體、論處所、論據、論莊嚴、論負、論出離、論多所作法。當知此中略有七種。一、論體性，二、論處所，三、論所依，四、論莊嚴，五、論墮負，六、論出離，七、論多所作法。
items.en: The science of medicine has now been explained. What is the science of logic? It refers to all the matters bound up in examining a meaning to be established. What, again, does this comprise? A summary verse states: the nature of discourse, the venue of discourse, the basis of discourse, the adornment of discourse, discourse's defeat, discourse's release, and the methods of greatest use in discourse. Know that, briefly, there are seven kinds here: first, the nature of discourse; second, the venue of discourse; third, the basis of discourse; fourth, the adornment of discourse; fifth, discourse's defeat; sixth, discourse's release; and seventh, the methods of greatest use in discourse.

items.title: The Nature of Discourse (I): Verbal Discourse and Worldly-Esteemed Discourse

items.zh: 云何論體性？謂有六種。一、言論，二、尚論，三、諍論，四、毀謗論，五、順正論，六、教導論。
items.en: What is the nature of discourse? It has six kinds: first, verbal discourse; second, worldly-esteemed discourse; third, contentious discourse; fourth, discourse of denigration; fifth, discourse in accord with the right; and sixth, instructional discourse.

items.zh: 言論者，謂一切言說、言音、言詞，是名言論。尚論者，謂諸世間隨所應聞所有言論。
items.en: Verbal discourse: it refers to all speech, all vocal sound, and all words — this is called verbal discourse. Worldly-esteemed discourse: it refers to whatever discourse in the world is fit to be heeded.

items.title: The Nature of Discourse (II): Contentious Discourse

items.zh: 諍論者，謂或依諸欲所起。若自所攝諸欲，他所侵奪；若他所攝諸欲，自行侵奪；若所愛有情所攝諸欲，更相侵奪。或欲侵奪。若無攝受諸欲，謂歌舞戲笑等所攝，若倡女僕從等所攝；或為觀看，或為受用。
items.en: Contentious discourse: it may arise dependent on desired objects. Whether objects one holds are seized by another, or objects another holds are seized by oneself, or objects held by a being one cherishes are seized by each from the other — or merely the wish to seize them arises. Or it may concern objects held by no one in particular, such as those bound up with song, dance, and merriment, or with courtesans and attendants — whether the dispute is over watching them or over making use of them.

items.zh: 於如是等諸欲事中，未離欲者，為欲界貪所染污者，因堅執故、因縛著故、因耽嗜故、因貪愛故，發憤乖違。喜鬪諍者，興種種論、興怨害論，故名諍論。
items.en: In regard to sense matters such as these, those who are not free from desire, defiled by desire-realm greed, through firm clinging, through bondage, through indulgence, and through craving, become provoked and set against each other. Those who delight in quarrelling raise all kinds of discourse, discourse of enmity and harm; so it is called contentious discourse.

items.zh: 或依惡行所起。若自所作身語惡行，他所譏毀；若他所作身語惡行，自行譏毀；若所愛有情所作身語惡行，互相譏毀。
items.en: Or it may arise dependent on misdeeds. Whether misdeeds of body or speech committed by oneself are mocked and denigrated by another, or such misdeeds committed by another are mocked and denigrated by oneself, or such misdeeds committed by a being one cherishes are mocked and denigrated by each from the other.

items.zh: 於如是等行惡行中，願作未作諸惡行者，未離欲界貪瞋癡者，重貪瞋癡所拘蔽者，因堅執故、因縛著故、因耽嗜故、因貪愛故，更相憤發，懷染污心，互相乖違。喜鬪諍者，興種種論、興怨害論，故名諍論。
items.en: In regard to engaging in misconduct such as this, those who wish to commit misdeeds not yet committed, who are not free from desire-realm greed, anger, and delusion, and who are bound and obscured by heavy greed, anger, and delusion, through firm clinging, through bondage, through indulgence, and through craving, provoke one another and, with defiled minds, set themselves against each other. Those who delight in quarrelling raise all kinds of discourse, discourse of enmity and harm; so it is called contentious discourse.

items.zh: 或依諸見所起。謂薩迦耶見、斷見、無因見、不平等因見、常見、雨眾見等種種邪見，及餘無量諸惡見類。於如是諸見中，或自所攝，他所遮斷；或他所攝，自行遮斷；或所愛有情所攝，他正遮斷；或已遮斷；或欲攝受所未攝受。
items.en: Or it may arise dependent on views — the view of a real self in the aggregates, the view of annihilation, the view of no cause, the view of an unequal cause, the view of permanence, the view held by the followers of Varṣa, and other such wrong views without measure. Regarding such views: whether a view one holds is blocked by another, or a view another holds is blocked by oneself, or a view held by a being one cherishes is being blocked by another, or has already been blocked, or one wishes to draw another towards a view not yet accepted.

items.zh: 未離欲者，如前廣說。乃至興種種論、興怨害論，是名諍論。
items.en: In all such matters, one who has not become free of desire, who is stained by craving for the desire realm — through firm attachment, through bondage, through insatiable indulgence, through craving — grows resentful and falls into conflict. One who delights in quarreling gives rise to discourse of every kind, discourse meant to wound: this is called contentious discourse.

blocks.text: Today completes inner wisdom and opens two more of the five sciences: **medicine** (醫方明), presented through the four noble truths, and **logic** (因明), the Indian science of debate, presented in seven headings. Logic will occupy the rest of the fascicle.

The eight masteries again (Day 88). Master Cháng Bǎi: the liberations take objects of resolve; the masteries take objects to be subdued, turning large to small and small to large. Venerable Miào Jìng suspects a copyist's error where the text says "three bases" for "eight".

The nine fetters (Day 53). The nine abodes of beings: Venerable Miào Jìng: the seven stations of consciousness (Day 115) plus the gods without perception and the sphere of neither-perception. (The treatise defers details to the *Compendium of Topics*; Master Cháng Bǎi notes the *Pīxún jì* found they are not actually there.)

subs.head: Ten totalities, ten factors of the adept

blocks.text: The ten totalities (Day 88). The **ten factors of the adept** (十無學支): the eightfold path plus right liberation and right knowledge. Master Cháng Bǎi: the eightfold path spans the first three fruits, so two more factors distinguish the arhat. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "knowledge and vision of liberation" is subsequently attained wisdom, knowing one's own fruit.
With the tens, "inner wisdom" is complete.

The science of **medicine** has four skills: knowing the marks of illness, its cause, its elimination, and its prevention. Both teachers map them onto the four noble truths: the marks of illness are suffering; its cause, origin; its elimination, cessation; the cure, the path. The Buddha is often called the great physician.

Master Cháng Bǎi adds a Buddhist perspective on health: medicine is a worldly expedient, because "my great affliction is that I have a body". Only cutting ignorance ends illness for good. Still, a bodhisattva learns medicine, because it relieves real suffering.

The science of **logic** (因明, *hetuvidyā*) concerns "all the matters in examining a meaning". Master Cháng Bǎi: the meaning examined is the thesis; the matters are the reasons and examples that establish it. It has seven headings: the nature of discourse, its venue, its basis, its adornment, its defeat, its release, and the methods of greatest use. This treatise belongs to the "old logic", before Dignāga's reform, and recognises three means of valid knowledge: perception, inference, and scriptural authority.

Discourse is of six kinds. Verbal discourse is all speech (Master Cháng Bǎi: speech is essence, sound mark, words function). Worldly-esteemed discourse explains what people need and value. Contentious discourse arises over desires, over misdeeds, and over views. Disputes can arise even over things owned by no one, such as song and dance. Venerable Miào Jìng's example of a contested view, "an unequal cause": "everything has a cause; then where did God come from?"

quiz.q: How do the objects of the eight liberations and the eight bases of mastery differ, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: liberations take objects of resolve; masteries take objects to be subdued — turning large to small, small to large, many to few, few to many
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The liberations take objects of resolve; the bases of mastery take objects to be subdued — large made small, small made large, many made few, few made many." Venerable Miào Jìng: the liberations are cause, the masteries fruit.

quiz.q: The text says "three bases of mastery." What does Venerable Miào Jìng think of the word "three"?
options: he feels it is a copyist's error for "eight"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This word 'three' — I feel it is a miswritten character; 'eight' bases of mastery is right." The *Pixunji* he reads explains "three" via the three liberations; the English keeps "three."

quiz.q: How are the nine abodes of beings composed, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the seven stations of consciousness plus the perceptionless gods and the sphere of neither-perception
nine grades of the pure land
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The seven stations of consciousness, plus the gods without perception, plus neither-perception-nor-non-perception — that makes nine." The evil destinies are excluded as repugnant.

quiz.q: How are the ten factors of the adept formed, and what do the two added factors do, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the eightfold path plus right liberation and right knowledge — since the eight span the first three fruits, these two distinguish the adept from trainees
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The eightfold path extends to the first three fruits; to distinguish trainees, two more limbs — right liberation and right knowledge — are added, making the ten factors of the adept." They fall within the adept's five aggregates.

quiz.q: The four skills of medicine correspond to what, according to both teachers?
options: the four noble truths — the marks of illness are suffering, its cause origin, its elimination cessation, the preventive means the path
quiz.why: The treatise lists skill in the marks, the cause, the elimination, and the prevention of illness. Venerable Miào Jìng: "This is just the meaning of the four truths; using doctor and illness as an analogy is very fitting." Master Cháng Bǎi concurs.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi position medicine within the Dharma, and where is the root of illness?
options: only a worldly expedient — illness comes from having a body; only cutting ignorance ends it for good
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: medicine is a worldly expedient; at root, "my great affliction is that I have a body." Only by cutting off ignorance does one leave illness for good; otherwise one falls ill, recovers, and falls ill again.

quiz.q: Among disputes over views is "the view of an unequal cause." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: God — everything has a cause, yet God has none: an unequal cause
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Everything has a cause — then where did God come from? God has no cause; that is unequal." He adds that the Varṣa followers are the Sāṃkhya school, named for a founder born in the rainy season.
